props.gloss_en: one may stand to pray only from gravity of mind
one may not stand to pray directly from [deciding] a judgment
nor directly from a matter of halakha
but from a settled halakha
Abaye: a settled halakha is like R' Zeira's [on the daughters of Israel]
the daughters of Israel were stringent on themselves: even on seeing a drop of blood the size of a mustard seed they sit seven clean days for it
Rava: a settled halakha is like Rav Hoshaya's [on grain in its chaff]
a person may use artifice with his grain and bring it in in its chaff so that his animal may eat of it, and it is exempt from tithe
or say: a settled halakha is like Rav Huna's [in R' Ze'eira's name, on blood let from a consecrated animal]
one who lets blood from a consecrated animal: the blood is forbidden for benefit
and one commits me'ila [misuse of consecrated property] with it
the Rabbanan acted like our mishnah [rising to pray from gravity]
Rav Ashi acted like the baraita [rising to pray from a settled halakha]
one may not stand to pray from sadness
nor from laziness
nor from laughter
nor from conversation
nor from frivolity
nor from idle matters
but from the joy of a mitzva
likewise one should not take leave of his fellow from conversation
nor from laughter
nor from frivolity
nor from idle matters
but from a matter of halakha
for so we found with the early prophets, who closed their words with words of praise and consolation
for thereby he will remember him
Rav Kahana escorted Rav Shimi bar Ashi from Pum Nahara as far as the palm groves of Babylonia
is it true, what people say, that these palms of Babylonia have been here from Adam until now?

'a land through which no man passed and where no man [adam] dwelt' (Jer 2:6) -- if none passed, how could any dwell? rather: every land Adam decreed for settlement was settled, and every land he did not was not
Rav Mordechai escorted Rav Shimi bar Ashi from Hagronya as far as Bei Keifei
and some say: as far as Bei Dura
